title: Correct normal force (part 1)
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for the normal force in part (1) must be 20 N.

title: Correct normal force (part 2)
description: Essential: The student's final numerical answer for the normal force in part (2) must be 160 N.

title: Force balance on container
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply vertical force equilibrium to the container, relating the water's weight to the vertical components of the contact forces from the blocks.

title: Newton's third law application
description: Important: The student must correctly state that the force the container exerts on a block is equal in magnitude to the force the block exerts on the container.

title: Friction limit condition
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must correctly set up the condition for impending motion of block B, balancing horizontal forces including friction at its maximum value.

title: Trigonometric component resolution
description: Important: The solution must correctly resolve forces into components parallel and perpendicular to the inclined contact surfaces using the given sine and cosine of 53°.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All forces should be expressed with correct units (Newtons) and intermediate calculations should maintain dimensional consistency.

title: Sign error in friction
description: Pitfall: Deduct points if the direction of the friction force on block B is incorrectly assigned or its sign is wrong in the horizontal force balance.

title: Incorrect mass or angle use
description: Pitfall: Deduct points if the student uses the wrong mass (e.g., block mass instead of water mass) or incorrect trigonometric values in a critical calculation.
